changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 3 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/11483-metric-card-needs-value.md`

- names `content/docs/plugins/plugin-dashboard.mdx` → `content/docs/plugins/plugin-dashboard.mdx` — edited by this change

  > - **What changed.** `DashboardWidgetTypeSchema` is now the spec's families plus `list` and `custom`, so the slot reads a `metric-card` through its component arm alone. The TypeScript twin, `DashboardWidgetTypeName`, drops `DashboardComponentWidgetType` the same way. `DASHBOARD_COMPONENT_WIDGET_TYPES` still lists `metric-card`: it is the component arm's `type`, and only that. - **What now refuses that did not.** Directly in `widgets[]`, both faces refuse a `metric-card` with no `value`. That holds whatever else the card carries: `title`, `description`, `id` and `layout`, a `dataset` with `values`, or its figure under `options` (`options: { value }`), which the tolerant face accepted. On its own, `DashboardWidgetSchema` (zod) refuses `type: 'metric-card'` at `type`. On the TypeScript face, `'metric-card'` is no longer a `DashboardWidgetTypeName`, so assigning it to that type is a compile error. - **Why no widget key stands in for `value`.** This was measured through the real `DashboardRenderer` and `DashboardGridLayout`. A `dataset` makes the dashboard draw `DatasetWidget` in the card's place, by a rule that does not read the `type`; the card is never mounted. `options` is spread onto the node as literal props: a second spelling of `value`, not a binding. No other widget key reached the figure. - **What does not move.** On the TypeScript face, `DashboardWidgetSchema['type']` still includes `'metric-card'`. That interface is also the read type of every `widgets[]` entry, and the component arm stays assignable to it. So a `metric-card` literal with no `value` still compiles directly in `widgets[]`, while the validator refuses it on both faces. A `metric-card` in a widget's legacy `component` envelope is judged as before: there, the tolerant face's `BaseSchema` fallback still accepts a card that fails the arm. Every `metric-card` in the schema catalog, the READMEs and the docs fences carries its `value`. The one docs example that did not, under "TypeScript Support" in `content/docs/plugins/plugin-dashboard.mdx`, is rewritten.

### `.changeset/8114-detail-tab-activity-timeline.md`

- names `plugin-dashboard/README.md` → `packages/plugin-dashboard/README.md` — edited by this change

  > `README.md` ships in this package's `files`, so the example went out in every tarball. `DetailTabs` renders a tab's `content` through `ANGLE-BRACKETS(SchemaRenderer schema={toRenderableSchema(tab.content)} /)`, which makes `content.type` an SDUI node position judged by the component registry — so a reader copying the tab got the registry's `Unknown component type` panel (OBJUI-001) where the timeline should be. Same shape as the `line-chart` widget in `plugin-dashboard/README.md` (objectui#7896's census; fixed by objectui#7951) and the fourth known instance.

### `.changeset/8760-unfulfilled-chart-stubs.md`

- names `content/docs/plugins/plugin-dashboard.mdx` → `content/docs/plugins/plugin-dashboard.mdx` — edited by this change

  > - **At render.** `SchemaRenderer`'s lazy branch re-checks `hasLazy(type)` on every pass and returns the `Loading ANGLE-BRACKETS(type)…` placeholder. `Registry.register()` deletes a lazy entry only for keys the loaded module actually registers, so for an unfulfilled key the entry SURVIVES the load and every later pass takes the same branch. Measured on `b775500af` through the real chain: `{ "type": "line-chart" }` painted `role="status"` / `data-lazy-loading="line-chart"` / `Loading line-chart…`, permanently. **Not** the `OBJUI-001` panel the card expected — no alert, no error, no console warning. A skeleton that never resolves reads to a user as a slow network. - **At authoring.** A stub is enough to put a key into `getKnownTypes()`, so `check:doc-types` and the CLI's generated `KNOWN_SCHEMA_TYPES` snapshot both blessed all three. `content/docs/plugins/plugin-dashboard.mdx` taught `"type": "line-chart"` inside a `card` body, and every gate was green on it.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Angle-bracketed names in the quoted prose above are rewritten as `ANGLE-BRACKETS(name)`: GitHub deletes tag-shaped fragments from a stored body, and a quote that silently loses the identifier it is about is worse than a visible repair.

Compared the checked-out tree with `8bfc0012e` (merge-base with origin/main): 9 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 2068 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2700 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/37095956158)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `29b4ab282b7e7ff20cccdeb8c176fe25bcd24e66`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card objectui#11525 (body and all four comments: ruling `5964914121`, claim `5965174453`, dev report `5965452133`, seat answer `5965464762`), PR #11538 (body, 11-file list, net diff against `main`), the head tree (one tarball GET, read as text), and the head's check-runs read twice (04:20:58Z and 04:27:03Z). Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The retirement, both surfaces — RIGHT.** `DashboardRenderer`'s metric arm (head line 869) and `DashboardGridLayout`'s (head line 382) return the imported `LEGACY_RETIRED_WIDGET_SCHEMA` when `isObjectProvider(widgetData)`, with `widgetData = widget.data || options.data`. The arm is `dispatch.family === 'metric'`, so it serves every member of `METRIC_LIKE_TYPES` (`metric`, `gauge`, `solid-gauge`, `kpi`, `bullet`); a typeless entry resolves to `metric` through `resolveWidgetType` on both surfaces, and the renderer's mobile metric row renders through the same `renderWidget`, so there is no third path. This is the ruled path (`5964914121`: both surfaces, the existing placeholder, as the pivot arm already does). Reaching the whole single-value family is right, not over-reach: the family arm WAS the producer, and retiring `type: 'metric'` alone would leave `gauge`/`kpi`/… building the undeclared node the ruling exists to remove.
2. **The producer is gone — RIGHT, and no accept set moves.** The flat `object-metric` node with its ObjectQL-dialect `filter` is removed from both arms. At the head no non-test source under `packages/` or `apps/` spells a `type: 'object-metric'` node literal except the kept union member type in `DashboardRenderer.tsx:188`. The diff touches no zod or TS face; `@object-ui/types` is untouched; the package's exports are unchanged.
3. **Confinement — RIGHT.** The series arms (renderer 774, grid 306) and table arms (renderer 917, grid 411) are not in the diff and keep their `isObjectProvider` branches; the pivot arms are unchanged; `isLegacyRetiredWidget` is unchanged. A dataset-bound metric is unaffected because the render-site `datasetBound` fork picks `DatasetWidget` on both surfaces regardless of what `getComponentSchema` returns; the static-metric branch follows the early return and still builds `DASHBOARD_NODE_TYPES.metric`.
4. **The kept broadcast member — RIGHT, justified by measurement.** `FilterableComponentType` / `FILTERABLE_COMPONENT_TYPES` keep `object-metric`. At the head `getComponentSchema` returns the envelope's node first (`entryComponent` → `toRenderableSchema(toDashboardNodeType(…))`, line 711) and the merge at 1028-1031 applies `isFilterableComponentSchema` to that return, so an authored legacy `component` envelope holding an `object-metric` node still reaches the merge. The pin asserts the node's `filter` equals `{ region: 'EMEA' }` and that `aggregate` is called. The claim's own condition ("removed where nothing else reads them") was measured not met; the seat accepted (`5965464762`). The type is module-private, so no public surface moves.
5. **Chrome — RIGHT, nothing moved.** `isSelfContained = entryType === 'metric' && !datasetBound` (renderer 1047, grid 624) is untouched: a retired `metric` or typeless tile draws the placeholder without the Card heading, exactly as the retired legacy top-level `object` metric tile already does (the DOM-equality pin holds the two equal), while `gauge`/`solid-gauge`/`kpi`/`bullet` take the Card heading, as the pivot does.
6. **Text that follows the code — RIGHT.** `legacyRetiredWidget.ts` gets the dated, append-only correction the ruling names (lines 44-58; the detector itself unchanged, as the note says). The `ObjectMetricWidget.tsx` docblock, both render-site comments, the broadcast docblock, the two docs pages, the README comment and its accent-table row all describe the change as it is. One cross-file line address in the edited grid paragraph became a symbol citation; `Line Citation Gate` is green.
7. **Pins — RIGHT.** `inlineObjectMetricRetired-11525.test.tsx`: 29 tests through the real `SchemaRenderer` behind a recording listener; subjects read off `METRIC_LIKE_TYPES` with a non-vacuity check, plus widget-level `data` and a typeless widget; the placeholder checked by identity, `object-metric` nodes counted zero, no `aggregate`/`find`/`queryDataset` call; controls for the pivot arm, the dataset-bound metric (`510000`), the static metric, the provider bar, the provider table and the envelope broadcast. The dev's reverse verification reads 16 red / 13 green at base, the stated direction. The objectui#4612 grid header gets a dated note; its provider control is a `bar`, so it stands.

**Check-runs on the head** (42). Second read, 04:27:03Z: 32 `success`, 3 `skipped` (the two coverage jobs and `dependabot`), 0 failure, 7 `in_progress`: `Test (shard 1/8, 3/8, 4/8, 5/8, 6/8, 7/8)` and `Spec Main Shape Gate`. Green and completed include `Type Check`, `Lint`, `Test (shard 2/8)`, `Test (shard 8/8)`, `Test (dist pins)`, `Build & E2E`, `Build Docs`, `Changeset Bump Policy`, `Changeset Fixed Group Check`, `Changeset Declaration`, `Changeset Claim Re-read`, `Changeset Overwrite Report`, `Line Citation Gate`, `Doc Snippet Type Check`, `Doc Example Id Check`, `Doc Component Type Check`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. Nothing red bears on the contract; the pending shards and the shape gate are landing gates the merge queue holds on, and they do not change what the diff publishes.

### ② Semver level

- **`.changeset/11525-inline-metric-retired.md` — `@object-ui/plugin-dashboard: minor` — RIGHT.** The diff publishes a behaviour change in the package's render of stored metadata: on both surfaces a stored dataset-less `provider: 'object'` single-value tile stops drawing its number and draws the rebind prompt. That is breaking for stored dashboards, so not `patch`; `major` is refused by `check-changeset-no-major` and the one fixed group; the house spelling for a retired render path is `minor` with the break stated (`7353`, `9165`, `retire-options-shorthand-lift-4356`; `10528`'s `patch` was the grid catching up to the renderer, not a retirement of a drawing path). The entry states the before (both surfaces aggregated and drew the number), the after (the exact placeholder text, no query), the fix (set `dataset`, select `values`), names all six forms (`metric`, `gauge`, `solid-gauge`, `kpi`, `bullet`, typeless) and both data spellings, and lists what does not move (chart and table arms, static metric, both faces, the envelope member). `Changeset Fixed Group Check` and `Changeset Bump Policy` are green.
- **The claim's line `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` — RIGHT.** The value answers whether the card widens an accept set or a public surface: no — no validator face moves, `@object-ui/types` is untouched, both faces already refuse a dataset-less widget, and the diff exports nothing new. The arm names the breaking direction: the fleet's reader defines `no (narrowing)` as "not a widening, but breaking", which is exactly a render retirement with no validator move. The dev's `tests` and the changeset carry the break in words.
- **Pending-changeset sweep, read not recalled.** `.changeset` tree `3e286b3f878c64e1284300a2bff786477c1dd724` at the head, listed from the git tree: 2,702 entries (2,701 `.md` plus `config.json`), not truncated. Every entry was swept as text for the four descriptions (an inline provider metric drawing its number or an `object-metric` node built for it; the nested provider config live for every family; "every widget that names a known family draws as before"; the filter broadcast reaching an inline metric), and the forty-odd hits were read in full.
  - **False, and noted — `11514-dashboard-slot-entry-types.md`.** Its "Every widget that names a known family draws as before" bullet no longer holds for this form. The PR appends a dated note in the house form (date, title, card, what held then, what holds now, the pointer to the 11525 entry, "the rest is kept as the reading"); frontmatter unchanged; `Changeset Overwrite Report` green (case 2).
